analysis:
This PR is documentation and changelog only: changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md (added) and docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3, new paragraph after head line 251). No source code is supplied, so no security control is changed in the evidence reviewed.

The docs describe a behavioral change in the SSD prefix-cache restore path (T-041, TB-007, A-001). Provider-staged complete-checkpoint imports now create destination arrays 'already available from host bytes' and never evaluate or fence them. This avoids blocking on MLX's process-wide evalLock while the engine prefills another request. The implementation, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and the ssd-kv-cache.md destination contract, is NOT in the supplied evidence.

Unverified contracts for the next pass, if the code diff is in another batch:
(1) Authentication still precedes use. DBK3 AES-GCM and AAD verification, salt-scoped HMAC lookup and weightHash/layoutEpoch bindings must be fully verified before host bytes are exposed as available arrays.
(2) Host-backed destination arrays must be lifetime-safe. They must not alias a buffer that is reused, unmapped or zeroed, and must not leave residual plaintext KV in host memory after the request (T-028, T-014).
(3) Skipping the eval or fence must not let a request read a partially restored, wrong-scope or cross-tenant checkpoint.
(4) Staging reservations through GlobalKVCacheBudget must still be released on the new path (SSDPrefixCache.endAdoption/completeStaging).
(5) The changelog claims faster contended restore. That does not widen the SEC-035 TTFT oracle in kind, but it could reduce hit/miss timing noise. This is a minor, accepted-risk consideration.

No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by the docs alone. Evidence for the code change is missing, so no finding is raised. Deeper review is recommended only if the corresponding Swift/SDK changes exist outside this batch.
